name: What We Learn(ed) from Rainbows
description:
What can rainbows teach us about physics and mathematics?

As well as describing the beautiful physics of a dramatic natural phenomenon, rainbow studies over several centuries have uncovered unexpected connections with other areas of physics and the practice of science more generally. The connections encompass the rainbow as an illusion—there is no arc in the sky—rainbow-related waves in water, and the historical role of rainbows in shaping colour theory.

These connections extend even further, to the deeper conceptual transition from ray to wave optics. The talk will explore a variety of physics concepts, from wave optics to quantum mechanics, and how they link to rainbows: the universal wave decoration of smooth focal lines, decoherence—wave interference blurred by imperfect resolution, and Gell-Mann’s totalitarian principle.

Finally, the lecture will explore how rainbow bridges physics and advanced mathematics, serving as a laboratory for numerical experimentation when analytical solutions are insufficient and delve into the mathematics of divergent series.

name: (QUANTUM) Science Writing
description:
How do you make science accessible without losing its depth?

Quantum physics has reshaped how we think about reality, technology, and the limits of what we can know. But how do we communicate these ideas beyond the laboratory—to readers, audiences, and communities who may not have a scientific background?
 
This panel brings together Jacob Koshy, Prathmesh Kher, and Chethan Kumar to explore the challenges and possibilities of engaging the public with quantum science. The conversation will look at the craft of science writing, the role of storytelling and journalism, and the choices involved in making unfamiliar and often counterintuitive ideas accessible without losing their complexity.
 
Join us for a conversation about who gets to tell stories about science, how those stories shape public understanding, and how we can make the quantum world a little less mysterious and a lot more engaging.

name: Qua?
description:
Every question in this quiz will have a connection to our QUANTUM exhibition—but don’t expect a physics exam. You’ll need to spot patterns, make connections, think sideways, and occasionally take a wild guess.

Whether you’re a schoolkid who asks too many questions, a lifelong learner, or a retired person who still wonders how the world works, this one’s for you. Just bring your curiosity.

name: Quantum Mechanics, Black Holes and Relativity
description:
What happens to very small black holes and what does this teach us about fundamental physics?

Our mundane notions of space and time are challenged by the theory of relativity that is important at high speeds or in the presence of strong gravitational fields.  On the other hand, quantum mechanics describes the physics of very small systems and forces us to refine our notion of reality. What if both gravity and quantum mechanics are important, as would happen for a very small black hole? Thinking about these systems leads us to very fascinating physics.

name: QUANTUM Trails
description: Step beyond the visible and into the world of QUANTUM. Join our Experimentors, Deepak and Aizaz, as they trace the connections between science, art and imagination. Discover the stories and ideas behind the works and experience the many strange, playful and thought-provoking ways quantum phenomena come to life.

name: Pralay: Game the Climate
description:
Can you win an election while saving the world, or will the chaos gods decide your fate?

Step into a fictionalised world grappling with a climate crisis in Pralay, a unique political strategy board game that blends science, creativity, and storytelling. Navigate competing social, cultural, economic, and environmental trade-offs as you contest for maximum votes to become the president of the new world government. Will you be able to win the election whilst keeping your people happy and saving the planet? Join the Pralay team for an afternoon of navigating complex climate decisions and experiencing how your choices shape the world.

name: Quantum Peekaboo: To See or Not to See
description:
The microscopic world operates on rules vastly different from what we expect. Molecules, atoms, and subatomic particles can seemingly exist in multiple locations at once and pass through barriers. The fates of distant particles appear spookily entangled. In this quantum jungle, randomness and probability replace certainty, defying our everyday intuition.

What makes the quantum realm so different from our macroscopic experience? In this lecture, Sushant will ask quantum systems the age-old question, "Who are you when nobody's watching?" to uncover the root of quantum weirdness.

name: Einstein's Clocks: The Place of Time
description:
This edition of Co-Read will explore Peter Galison’s seminal article, *Einstein's Clocks: The Place of Time*.

Join us to understand how time not only confounded Einstein during his work at the patent office, but also shaped his thought experiments. We will look at how political imaginations, scientific theories, and everyday machines shaped one another in Germany at the turn of the 20th century. Along the way, the discussion may even introduce you to some key concepts in the philosophy of science.

name: Designing the Future
description:
How can art help us imagine possible futures?

Join Abel Korinsky for a collaborative crafting session, exploring how familiar materials and technologies might evolve into unexpected forms of life. Observe how everyday elements of the technosphere, be it plastic, electronics, or sensors, already shape our world and then speculate on what they could become.

Experimenting with motors, recycled plastics, and found materials, you will build a small moving organism of the future. Your speculative creatures might adapt to pollution, communicate with machines, survive in extreme environments, or develop entirely new relationships with humans and ecosystems.

name: (Observing) a Quantum Cat
description: The concept of quantum superposition is famously strange. Can something be two things at once until we look? How do you make sense of an idea that changes the moment you observe it, or explain it to someone meeting it for the first time? From the exhibiting artists of *Sticking with Light*, this workshop will take you through superposition using light, colour, polarisers, and a cat that refuses to make up its mind.

name: Piece by Piece
description:
Puzzled by quantum? You’re in the right place. Join us for a relaxed afternoon to piece together quantum inspired puzzles of cats, wormholes, iridescence and more. You can also solve puzzles of beautiful images and even get a little competitive with some speed puzzling! 

Puzzles are for everyone: come alone, with a partner, or with friends and family!

name: Visualising Quantum Mechanics
description:
Quantum mechanics, like all of physics, aims to predict what happens, albeit in a probabilistic manner.  But what does it actually mean?  What is happening under the surface? Moving through a visual essay in your browser, you will examine this gap during the workshop. 

Vivek Vaidya will guide you through the hidden aspects of the double-slit experiment, decoherence, Bohm’s pilot wave, and the many-worlds interpretation. Between each topic, you play: aim a wavefunction at a target you cannot strike directly, read a barrier from a quantum-potential landscape, or herd thirty-two worlds that repel one another. The games use the same solvers as the essay figures, so the intuitions you develop reflect the physics.
